DSS  ·  ORIT GE'EZ  ·  MASORETIC VARIANT  ·  CRITICAL NOTE

YHWH / 𐤑𐤄𐤅𐤑 and The Creator only — no substitutions

All personal names in original Hebrew form throughout

THE OPPRESSION IN EGYPT — CHAPTERS 1 THROUGH 4

SHEMOT — CHAPTER 1 The Children of Yisra'el Multiply — The Oppression Begins

1:1 Now these are the names of the sons of Yisra'el who came to Mitzrayim with Ya'akov, each with his household:

1:2 Re'uven, Shim'on, Levi, and Yehudah,

1:3 Yissakhar, Zevulun, and Binyamin,

1:4 Dan and Naftali, Gad and Asher.

1:5 And all the souls who came out of the loins of Ya'akov were seventy souls; and Yosef was already in Mitzrayim.

1:6 Then Yosef died, and all his brothers, and all that generation.

1:7 But the children of Yisra'el were fruitful and swarmed and multiplied and grew exceedingly mighty, so that the land was filled with them.

1:8 Now there arose a new king over Mitzrayim, who did not know Yosef.

1:9 And he said to his people: Behold, the people of the children of Yisra'el are more numerous and mightier than we are.

1:10 Come, let us deal shrewdly with them, lest they multiply, and it happen that when war breaks out, they join themselves also to our enemies and fight against us, and go up out of the land.

1:11 So they set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens; and they built for Pharaoh store-cities, Pitom and Ra'amses.

1:12 But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and the more they spread abroad; and the Egyptians came to dread the children of Yisra'el.

1:13 And Mitzrayim made the children of Yisra'el serve with rigor,

1:14 and made their lives bitter with hard service — in mortar and in bricks, and in all manner of labor in the field, all their service in which they made them serve with rigor.

1:15 And the king of Mitzrayim said to the Hebrew midwives — one of whom was named Shifrah, and the other Puah —

1:16 When you serve as midwife to the Hebrew women and see them on the birthstool: if it is a son, you shall kill him; but if it is a daughter, she shall live.

1:17 But the midwives feared the Creator, and did not do as the king of Mitzrayim commanded them; they let the boys live.

1:18 So the king of Mitzrayim called for the midwives and said to them: Why have you done this thing, and let the boys live?

1:19 And the midwives said to Pharaoh: Because the Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women — they are vigorous, and give birth before the midwife comes to them.

1:20 So the Creator dealt well with the midwives; and the people multiplied and grew very mighty.

1:21 And because the midwives feared the Creator, he gave them families.

1:22 Then Pharaoh commanded all his people, saying: Every son that is born, you shall cast into the Nile; but every daughter you shall let live.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4QExodb (4Q13) preserves Exodus 1:5 — VERIFIED via a directly-quoted, line-numbered critical-edition transcription (Lexham Press, 2010, based on DJD XII), whose bracket notation shows the number is physically preserved ink, not editorial reconstruction: חמש ושבעים נפש, "seventy-five souls," against MT's "seventy." A second witness, 4Q1 (4QGen-Exoda), is PROBABLE for the same reading at the parallel Genesis 46:27. 4Q14 (span Exod 7–18) and 4QpaleoExodm/4Q22 (span Exod 6:25–37:16) are confirmed not to reach this chapter.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The Samaritan Pentateuch was checked verse-by-verse for this chapter via a dedicated SP/MT comparison index, which flags no variant anywhere in Exodus 1. At 1:5 specifically, SP reads שבעים ("seventy"), PROBABLE per converging citation — agreeing with MT, against the DSS/LXX "seventy-five" above.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verse 1:7 — the children of Yisra'el were fruitful and swarmed and multiplied and grew exceedingly mighty, echoing the creation blessing of Bereshit 1:28 and the covenant blessings to Avraham, Yitzhak, and Ya'akov. (Corrected August 4, 2026: this note previously carried wording inherited from the pre-reconstruction Reader text — "the people of Yisra'el were fruitful and increased greatly" — rather than the reconstruction's own literal rendering, which retains the vivid verb "swarmed" from וישרצו. Wording only was corrected; the underlying thematic observation is unchanged.)

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verse 1:16 — "the birthstool" translates על־האבנים, literally "upon the two stones" (a dual form), a documented lexical crux between a birthing-seat reading (majority) and a potter's-wheel euphemism (minority).

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verse 1:17 — the midwives feared The Creator, not Pharaoh — the first act of resistance in Shemot, performed by two named women, Shifrah and Puah.

SHEMOT — CHAPTER 2 The Birth of Moshe — Midyan

2:1 Now a man of the house of Levi went and took a daughter of Levi as his wife.

2:2 The woman conceived and bore a son; and when she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him three months.

2:3 When she could hide him no longer, she took for him a basket of bulrushes and coated it with bitumen and pitch; she put the child in it and set it among the reeds by the bank of the Nile.

2:4 And his sister stood at a distance, to know what would be done to him.

2:5 Then the daughter of Pharaoh came down to bathe at the Nile, while her attendants walked beside the river. She saw the basket among the reeds and sent her maid to fetch it.

2:6 When she opened it, she saw the child — behold, a boy, crying. She had compassion on him and said: This is one of the Hebrews' children.

2:7 Then his sister said to Pharaoh's daughter: Shall I go and call for you a nurse from the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for you?

2:8 And Pharaoh's daughter said to her: Go. So the girl went and called the child's mother.

2:9 Pharaoh's daughter said to her: Take this child away and nurse him for me, and I will give you your wages. So the woman took the child and nursed him.

2:10 When the child grew up, she brought him to Pharaoh's daughter, and he became her son; she called his name Moshe, and said: Because I drew him out of the water.

2:11 In those days, when Moshe had grown up, he went out to his brothers and looked on their burdens; and he saw an Egyptian striking a Hebrew, one of his brothers.

2:12 He looked this way and that way, and when he saw there was no one, he struck down the Egyptian and hid him in the sand.

2:13 When he went out the second day, behold, two Hebrew men were fighting; and he said to the one in the wrong: Why do you strike your fellow?

2:14 And he said: Who made you a ruler and a judge over us? Do you intend to kill me as you killed the Egyptian? Then Moshe was afraid, and said: Surely the matter is known.

2:15 When Pharaoh heard of this matter, he sought to kill Moshe. But Moshe fled from Pharaoh and settled in the land of Midyan; and he sat down by a well.

2:16 Now the priest of Midyan had seven daughters; and they came and drew water and filled the troughs to water their father's flock.

2:17 Then shepherds came and drove them away; but Moshe stood up and helped them, and watered their flock.

2:18 When they came to Re'uel their father, he said: How is it that you have come so quickly today?

2:19 They said: An Egyptian delivered us from the hand of the shepherds; he even drew water for us and watered the flock.

2:20 He said to his daughters: And where is he? Why is it that you left the man? Call him, that he may eat bread.

2:21 Moshe was content to dwell with the man; and he gave Tzipporah his daughter to Moshe.

2:22 She bore a son, and he called his name Gershom; for he said: I have been a stranger in a foreign land.

2:23 During that long period, the king of Mitzrayim died. The children of Yisra'el groaned because of the bondage, and they cried out; and their cry for help rose up to the Creator because of the bondage.

2:24 And the Creator heard their groaning, and the Creator remembered his covenant with Avraham, with Yitzhak, and with Ya'akov.

2:25 And the Creator saw the children of Yisra'el, and the Creator knew.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4QExodb (4Q13) preserves Exodus 2 within its confirmed span (Exod 1–5). VERIFIED, via a directly-quoted peer-reviewed critical study (Terry C. Iles, "Exegetical Variation in Exodus 2," Perichoresis 23.1, 2025, itself citing DJD XII): at 2:3, 4Q13 contains a narrative expansion absent from MT — a reference to Moshe's mother instructing "her slave-girl" (שפחתה) to "go" (לכי), language the study identifies as drawn forward from Pharaoh's daughter's "Go!" to Moshe's sister at v.8a in MT. This specific variant is the subject of a dedicated 2002 study (Rofé, DSD 9: 38–43). The exact full wording carries residual paleographic uncertainty inherent to the fragment's damaged state; the existence of the expansion is confirmed, its complete text is not fully clean. 4Q14 (span Exod 7–18) and 4QpaleoExodm/4Q22 (span Exod 6:25–37:16) remain confirmed absent from this chapter, as established for chapter 1.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The Septuagint shows two coordinated Greek translation choices across this chapter's episodes — ἄρσεν ("male") linking 1:16, 22, 2:2, 10; ἀναιρέω ("take up"/"destroy") linking 2:5, 10, 14–15, using the same Greek root for both Moshe's rescue from the water and his killing of the Egyptian. These are translator-technique observations, not Hebrew textual variants. Separately, at 2:22, the study identifies an actual Hebrew Vorlage-level difference behind the LXX at this point; independently, many later LXX witnesses (plus the Vulgate, Syriac, Coptic, and Arabic — no Hebrew manuscript) add an Eliezer-naming clause here, imported from Exodus 18:4. None of this is adopted into the ACR rendering; MT's shorter text at 2:22 stands.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The Samaritan Pentateuch was checked against the same dedicated comparison index used for chapter 1. No significant variant was identified through the checked sources for chapter 2 — consistent with broader scholarship that SP's major expansions concentrate in the plague narratives (Exodus 6–11) and the Decalogue (Exodus 20), not this chapter.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verse 2:10 — the name משה is explained via the Hebrew root משה, "to draw out." This Hebrew folk-etymology, as narrated in the text itself, is preserved directly; a separate, non-competing scholarly observation notes the name's likely Egyptian linguistic origin (a common element in Egyptian royal names such as Ramesses), which is not adopted into the translation but is worth recording as background.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verses 2:23–25 close the chapter with four distinct verbs of divine attention in sequence — heard, remembered, saw, knew — rendered as four separate acts rather than compressed into one, preserving the passage's own escalating structure.

SHEMOT — CHAPTER 3 The Burning Bush — The Name Revealed

3:1 Now Moshe was keeping the flock of Yitro his father-in-law, the priest of Midyan; he led the flock to the far side of the wilderness, and came to the mountain of the Creator, to Horev.

3:2 And the angel of YHWH appeared to him in a flame of fire from the midst of a bush; he looked, and behold, the bush was burning with fire, yet the bush was not consumed.

3:3 Moshe said: I will turn aside now and see this great sight — why the bush does not burn up.

3:4 When YHWH saw that he turned aside to look, the Creator called to him from the midst of the bush and said: Moshe, Moshe! And he said: Here I am.

3:5 And he said: Do not come near; take your sandals off your feet, for the place on which you stand is holy ground.

3:6 He said further: I am the Creator of your father, the Creator of Avraham, the Creator of Yitzhak, and the Creator of Ya'akov. And Moshe hid his face, for he was afraid to look at the Creator.

3:7 And YHWH said: I have surely seen the affliction of my people who are in Mitzrayim, and have heard their cry because of their taskmasters; for I know their sufferings.

3:8 I have come down to deliver them from the hand of Mitzrayim, and to bring them up out of that land to a good and spacious land, a land flowing with milk and honey — to the place of the Kena'ani, the Hitti, the Emori, the Perizzi, the Hivi, and the Yevusi.

3:9 And now, behold, the cry of the children of Yisra'el has come to me; and I have also seen the oppression with which Mitzrayim oppresses them.

3:10 Come now, and I will send you to Pharaoh, that you may bring my people, the children of Yisra'el, out of Mitzrayim.

3:11 But Moshe said to the Creator: Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh, and that I should bring the children of Yisra'el out of Mitzrayim?

3:12 And he said: I will surely be with you; and this shall be the sign to you that I have sent you — when you have brought the people out of Mitzrayim, you shall serve the Creator on this mountain.

3:13 Then Moshe said to the Creator: Behold, when I come to the children of Yisra'el and say to them, The Creator of your fathers has sent me to you, and they say to me, What is his name? — what shall I say to them?

3:14 And the Creator said to Moshe: I Will Be What I Will Be. And he said: Thus you shall say to the children of Yisra'el — I Will Be has sent me to you.

3:15 And the Creator said further to Moshe: Thus you shall say to the children of Yisra'el — YHWH, the Creator of your fathers, the Creator of Avraham, the Creator of Yitzhak, and the Creator of Ya'akov, has sent me to you. This is my name forever, and this is my memorial to all generations.

3:16 Go and gather the elders of Yisra'el, and say to them: YHWH, the Creator of your fathers, appeared to me — the Creator of Avraham, Yitzhak, and Ya'akov — saying: I have surely attended to you, and seen what is done to you in Mitzrayim.

3:17 And I have said: I will bring you up out of the affliction of Mitzrayim to the land of the Kena'ani, the Hitti, the Emori, the Perizzi, the Hivi, and the Yevusi — to a land flowing with milk and honey.

3:18 And they will listen to your voice; and you shall come, you and the elders of Yisra'el, to the king of Mitzrayim, and you shall say to him: YHWH, the Creator of the Hebrews, has met with us; and now, please let us go three days' journey into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to YHWH our Creator.

3:19 But I know that the king of Mitzrayim will not let you go, except by a mighty hand.

3:20 So I will stretch out my hand and strike Mitzrayim with all my wonders which I will do in its midst; and after that he will let you go.

3:21 And I will give this people favor in the sight of Mitzrayim; and it shall be, when you go, you will not go empty-handed.

3:22 But every woman shall ask of her neighbor, and of her who sojourns in her house, articles of silver and articles of gold, and clothing; and you shall put them on your sons and on your daughters, and you shall plunder Mitzrayim.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4QExodb (4Q13)'s confirmed span (Exodus 1–5) includes this chapter. CONFIRMED at the span level; no chapter-3-specific variant was located this session, so verse-level content is UNVERIFIED / OPEN rather than either claimed or denied. 4Q1 (4QGen-Exoda)'s coverage of this chapter is likewise UNVERIFIED / OPEN. 4Q14 and 4QpaleoExodm/4Q22 remain confirmed absent (spans Exod 7–18 and Exod 6:25–37:16), as established for chapters 1–2.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] Verse 3:6 — MT reads אלהי אביך, "the God of your father" (singular). A dedicated SP/MT comparison source reports the Samaritan Pentateuch reads the plural, "the God of your fatherS." PROBABLE. Notably, Acts 7:32's quotation of this verse also uses the plural — a cited scholarly study (Richard, CBQ 1977) identifies this as closer to the Samaritan reading than to MT's singular. MT's singular is retained as the ACR base; the SP/Acts alignment is displayed as a separate observation.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verse 3:14 — the chapter's central translation event. MT's אהיה אשר אהיה is grammatically an imperfect (future/durative) verb form. The Septuagint renders it ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ὤν, "I am the one who is" — a present-tense, ontological framing. This is well-documented scholarly consensus as an interpretive translation choice, not a different Hebrew Vorlage: a literal rendering of the Hebrew imperfect would have been ἔσομαι ὃς ἔσομαι, "I will be who I will be," and later Jewish Greek revisers (Aquila, Theodotion) explicitly reverted to this future-tense form. The ACR rendering ("I Will Be What I Will Be") follows the Hebrew's own grammatical aspect rather than the LXX/Vulgate's later present-tense "I AM" tradition — a real, documented translation-tradition fork, recorded rather than silently resolved either way.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verses 3:2–4 — the figure is introduced as "the angel of YHWH" (v.2) but speaks and is addressed as YHWH/the Creator directly from v.4 onward. This fluidity between "the angel" and the divine speaker is a textual observation recorded here, not a theological claim resolved by this note.

SHEMOT — CHAPTER 4 The Signs — Aharon Appointed — The Return to Mitzrayim

4:1 Then Moshe answered and said: But behold, they will not believe me, nor listen to my voice; for they will say, YHWH has not appeared to you.

4:2 YHWH said to him: What is that in your hand? And he said: A staff.

4:3 And he said: Cast it on the ground. So he cast it on the ground, and it became a serpent; and Moshe fled from before it.

4:4 Then YHWH said to Moshe: Stretch out your hand and take it by the tail. So he stretched out his hand and took hold of it, and it became a staff in his hand —

4:5 that they may believe that YHWH, the Creator of their fathers, the Creator of Avraham, the Creator of Yitzhak, and the Creator of Ya'akov, has appeared to you.

4:6 YHWH said to him further: Put your hand into your bosom. So he put his hand into his bosom, and when he took it out, behold, his hand was leprous, like snow.

4:7 And he said: Put your hand back into your bosom. So he put his hand back into his bosom, and when he took it out of his bosom, behold, it was restored like the rest of his flesh.

4:8 And it shall be, if they will not believe you, nor heed the voice of the first sign, that they will believe the voice of the latter sign.

4:9 And it shall be, if they will not believe even these two signs, nor listen to your voice, that you shall take water from the river and pour it on the dry ground; and the water which you take from the river will become blood on the dry ground.

4:10 Then Moshe said to YHWH: O my Creator, I am not a man of words, neither before, nor since you have spoken to your servant; for I am slow of speech and slow of tongue.

4:11 And YHWH said to him: Who has made man's mouth? Or who makes him mute, or deaf, or seeing, or blind? Is it not I, YHWH?

4:12 Now therefore go, and I will be with your mouth, and teach you what you shall speak.

4:13 But he said: O my Creator, please send by the hand of whomever else you will send.

4:14 Then the anger of YHWH burned against Moshe, and he said: Is there not Aharon your brother, the Levite? I know that he can speak well. And behold, he is coming out to meet you; and when he sees you, he will be glad in his heart.

4:15 You shall speak to him and put the words in his mouth; and I will be with your mouth and with his mouth, and will teach you what you shall do.

4:16 He shall speak for you to the people; he shall be to you a mouth, and you shall be to him in the Creator's stead.

4:17 And you shall take in your hand this staff, with which you shall do the signs.

4:18 Then Moshe went and returned to Yeter his father-in-law, and said to him: Please let me go, and return to my brothers who are in Mitzrayim, and see whether they are still alive. And Yitro said to Moshe: Go in peace.

4:19 And YHWH said to Moshe in Midyan: Go, return to Mitzrayim, for all the men who sought your life are dead.

4:20 So Moshe took his wife and his sons and set them on a donkey, and he returned to the land of Mitzrayim; and Moshe took the staff of the Creator in his hand.

4:21 And YHWH said to Moshe: When you go to return to Mitzrayim, see that you do before Pharaoh all the wonders which I have put in your hand; but I will harden his heart, and he will not let the people go.

4:22 Then you shall say to Pharaoh: Thus says YHWH — Yisra'el is my son, my firstborn.

4:23 And I have said to you, Let my son go, that he may serve me; but you have refused to let him go. Behold, I will slay your son, your firstborn.

4:24 Now it came to pass on the way, at the lodging place, that YHWH met him and sought to kill him.

4:25 Then Tzipporah took a flint and cut off the foreskin of her son, and cast it at his feet, and said: Surely you are a bridegroom of blood to me.

4:26 So he let him alone. Then she said: A bridegroom of blood — because of the circumcision.

4:27 And YHWH said to Aharon: Go into the wilderness to meet Moshe. So he went, and met him at the mountain of the Creator, and kissed him.

4:28 And Moshe told Aharon all the words of YHWH with which he had sent him, and all the signs with which he had charged him.

4:29 Then Moshe and Aharon went and gathered all the elders of the children of Yisra'el.

4:30 And Aharon spoke all the words which YHWH had spoken to Moshe, and did the signs in the sight of the people.

4:31 And the people believed; and when they heard that YHWH had attended to the children of Yisra'el, and that he had seen their affliction, they bowed their heads and worshipped.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4QExodb (4Q13)'s confirmed span (Exodus 1–5) includes this chapter. CONFIRMED at the span level; no chapter-4-specific variant was located this session, so verse-level content is UNVERIFIED / OPEN. 4Q1's coverage of this chapter is likewise UNVERIFIED / OPEN. 4Q14 and 4QpaleoExodm/4Q22 remain confirmed absent (spans Exod 7–18 and Exod 6:25–37:16).

[MASORETIC VARIANT] Verses 4:24–26, the "bridegroom of blood" passage — one of the most difficult passages in the Torah; even within MT alone, scholarship is divided on whether YHWH sought to kill Moshe or the infant Gershom. A dedicated SP/MT comparison source reports the Samaritan Pentateuch reads this episode substantially differently: rather than a physical circumcision, SP has Tzipporah "circumcise her heart," a reading connected to Devarim 10:16's "circumcise your heart" language. PROBABLE, via a single dedicated secondary source, not cross-checked against a primary SP edition this session. MT's version is retained as the ACR base precisely because the two accounts differ enough that merging them would misrepresent both.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verse 4:24 — MT states plainly that YHWH met Moshe and sought to kill him. The Septuagint, along with Targum Onkelos and Arabic versions, renders the actor as "an angel of the LORD" rather than YHWH directly. Whether this reflects a different Hebrew Vorlage or an interpretive softening of a theologically difficult claim is not resolved by the sources consulted this session — recorded as an open classification question, not assigned to either category by default. This is the second instance in four chapters (see ch.3's note on the burning bush) where an intermediary "angel" figure appears at a point of direct divine action in some witnesses — an observed pattern, not a resolved theological claim.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verse 4:2 — the printed Masoretic text itself displays a Ketiv/Qere pair (מזה written, מה־זה traditionally read), an internal feature of the Masoretic scribal tradition rather than a cross-witness variant.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verse 4:16 — אלהים is used comparatively ("you shall be to him in the Creator's stead," describing Moshe's relative authority over Aharon), not as a direct divine-name occurrence. An earlier draft of this chapter's translation briefly rendered a different verse's אדני as "O my Lord" before this was caught and corrected to "O my Creator," consistent with the project's naming policy — recorded here as a disclosed self-correction, not smoothed over.

MOSHE BEFORE PHARAOH — THE TEN PLAGUES — CHAPTERS 5 THROUGH 12

SHEMOT — CHAPTER 5 Pharaoh Refuses — Bricks Without Straw

5:1 Afterward Moshe and Aharon came and said to Pharaoh: Thus says YHWH, the Creator of Yisra'el — Let my people go, that they may hold a feast to me in the wilderness.

5:2 But Pharaoh said: Who is YHWH, that I should heed his voice to let Yisra'el go? I do not know YHWH, and moreover I will not let Yisra'el go.

5:3 And they said: The Creator of the Hebrews has met with us. Please let us go three days' journey into the wilderness and sacrifice to YHWH our Creator, lest he fall upon us with pestilence or with the sword.

5:4 But the king of Mitzrayim said to them: Moshe and Aharon, why do you draw the people away from their work? Get to your burdens.

5:5 And Pharaoh said: Behold, the people of the land are now many, and you would have them rest from their burdens?

5:6 So that same day Pharaoh commanded the taskmasters of the people and their foremen, saying:

5:7 You shall no longer give the people straw to make bricks, as before; let them go and gather straw for themselves.

5:8 But the quota of bricks which they made before, you shall lay upon them; you shall not reduce it, for they are idle — therefore they cry out, saying, Let us go and sacrifice to our Creator.

5:9 Let heavier work be laid upon the men, that they may labor at it, and let them not regard lying words.

5:10 So the taskmasters of the people and their foremen went out and said to the people: Thus says Pharaoh — I will not give you straw.

5:11 Go yourselves, get straw wherever you can find it; for none of your work will be reduced.

5:12 So the people were scattered throughout all the land of Mitzrayim to gather stubble for straw.

5:13 And the taskmasters pressed them, saying: Complete your work, your daily task, as when there was straw.

5:14 And the foremen of the children of Yisra'el, whom Pharaoh's taskmasters had set over them, were beaten, and were asked: Why have you not fulfilled your quota of bricks, as before, both yesterday and today?

5:15 Then the foremen of the children of Yisra'el came and cried out to Pharaoh, saying: Why do you deal this way with your servants?

5:16 No straw is given to your servants, yet they say to us, Make bricks! And behold, your servants are beaten, but the fault is in your own people.

5:17 But he said: You are idle, idle! That is why you say, Let us go and sacrifice to YHWH.

5:18 Now therefore go, work; no straw will be given to you, yet you must deliver the quota of bricks.

5:19 And the foremen of the children of Yisra'el saw that they were in trouble, when they were told: You shall not reduce your daily quota of bricks.

5:20 And they met Moshe and Aharon, who stood waiting for them as they came out from Pharaoh.

5:21 And they said to them: May YHWH look upon you and judge, because you have made us stink in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of his servants, putting a sword in their hand to kill us.

5:22 Then Moshe returned to YHWH and said: O Creator, why have you dealt ill with this people? Why did you ever send me?
